text:
Carla (ACME): Hey team — hitting a regression with our streaming integration to Redwood. Using the gRPC->HTTP gateway (grpc-gateway) and clients on HTTP/1.1. We get partial SSE events then the connection drops; client reconnect logic sees duplicate partial messages. This started after a load balancer change last week.

Alice (Support): Sorry you're seeing that, Carla. Can you share a minimal repro (curl + headers) and error traces from the client? Also which LB / proxy are you sitting behind?

Carla (ACME): We're behind an nginx proxy (k8s ingress on GKE), then an internal gRPC-gateway service that converts streaming gRPC to text/event-stream to the browser. Repro:

curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://our-gateway.example.com/v1/stream?prompt=test

Runs for a few seconds, returns some events, then the socket closes with no final event. Browser console shows:
EventSource error: connection closed with partial data

Alice (Support): Thanks. Can you paste the raw response headers (with sensitive tokens redacted)?

Carla (ACME): From the gateway (redacted):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: no-cache
Connection: keep-alive

Alice (Support): Two immediate suspects: 1) an intermediary (nginx ingress / LB) is buffering chunked responses until the upstream finishes, producing long pauses/partial frames; 2) the grpc-gateway translation layer isn't flushing after each chunk, so clients see partial lines when the buffer is flushed.

Ben (eng-runtime): Adding some context — HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 differences matter here. With HTTP/2 we rely on DATA frames that can be pushed immediately; many HTTP/1.1 proxies will buffer small chunked writes and only flush when a TCP buffer fills or the upstream closes. That causes "bursty" delivery which breaks SSE reconcilers expecting fine-grained events. Also watch out for gRPC gateways that buffer to assemble gRPC chunk boundaries.

Sam (SRE): Also check upstream keepalive and idle timeouts: if nginx or a cloud LB closes an idle stream aggressively, clients may reconnect mid-event. For SSE you want long timeouts, and explicit flushes from upstream.

Carla (ACME): We can try switching to HTTP/2 end-to-end, but our client stack falls back to HTTP/1.1 and we can't force everyone to upgrade. Any quick mitigations?

Ben (eng-runtime): Quick checklist: 
- Ensure server flushes after each event (e.g., node: res.flush() or use chunked writes and call flush)
- For nginx ingress: disable proxy_buffering for the SSE path (proxy_buffering off;) or add header X-Accel-Buffering: no
- For Envoy: set buffer limits / disable response buffer for streaming routes (streaming_idle_timeout, max_response_headers_kb not blocking)
- For ALBs: Classic ALB/NGINX can buffer; consider NLB or TCP pass-through to avoid HTTP-level buffering
- Add keep-alive headers and long idle timeouts on LB layer

Alice (Support): Can you test with a direct curl to the Redwood endpoint (bypass grpc-gateway) so we can determine where buffering is introduced? Example:

# http/2 test
curl -v --http2-prior-knowledge -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/stream?prompt=test

# force http/1.1 via curl
curl -v --http1.1 -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/stream?prompt=test

Carla (ACME): Ran both. Direct to Redwood: HTTP/2 run is smooth, events arrive in steady stream. Forcing HTTP/1.1 directly to Redwood still shows intermittent batching but less severe than through our gateway. Going through our grpc-gateway + nginx shows the worst behavior.

Ben (eng-runtime): That strongly suggests buffering at the gateway/proxy. Two additional things to check in your grpc-gateway: are you using net/http ResponseWriter without calling Flush? Many implementations write chunks but rely on the framework to flush which some proxies won't honor. Also check if the gateway adds Content-Length mistakenly for certain responses — that will break chunking behavior.

Carla (ACME): Our gateway is Golang-based using grpc-gateway v2. It's using a streaming handler that does: writer.Write([]byte(event)); // no explicit Flush

Ben (eng-runtime): There's the issue — net/http will buffer unless you call http.Flusher.Flush() after each write. Also consider setting header "X-Accel-Buffering: no" from the gateway to hint nginx. Example snippet:

// pseudo
w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok { 
  f.Flush()
}

Carla (ACME): OK will try adding Flush and the header. Any non-invasive infra changes we can do while code change rolls out?

Sam (SRE): On nginx ingress you can patch the ingress rule for that path to add: proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade; or inject header as Ben suggested. Also bump proxy_read_timeout and keepalive. If behind GCLB, check backend streaming support; some LBs will buffer responses for HTTP/1.1.

infra-bot: Deployed config patch to staging ingress: added annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffering: "off" for path /v1/stream.

Carla (ACME): Staging test after the ingress annotation looks much better — events arrive steadily and the browser no longer sees partial duplicates. Production change pending.

Alice (Support): Great. Two followups for our records: 1) can you paste the small code diff (Flush + header) you pushed? 2) Which LB/proxy changed last week that triggered this? We want to correlate with release notes.

Carla (ACME): Diff (redacted):
- w.Write([]byte(fmtEvent))
+ w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
+ if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok { f.Flush() }
+ w.Write([]byte(fmtEvent))

Carla (ACME): The change was an upstream nginx helm chart bump that changed default proxy_buffering behavior for chunked responses.

Ben (eng-runtime): Marking this pattern as common — we'll add a short KB to docs for "SSE and HTTP/1.1 proxy buffering" covering: headers, nginx annotations, envoy streaming flags, and grpc-gateway flush best-practices. Also note recommendation to prefer HTTP/2 end-to-end where possible.

Sam (SRE): I'll schedule an infra postmortem to audit other ingress paths that might be affected.

Carla (ACME): Thanks everyone — will confirm once prod rollout is done. Much appreciated. :thumbsup:

Alice (Support): Leaving P1 -> resolved (workaround + code change + ingress annotation). Reopen if it recurs.

Ben (eng-runtime): Follow-up issue filed: INF-2482 "SSE buffering issues with grpc-gateway/nginx" with reproduction and KB draft.

Carla (ACME): FYI — final prod rollout completed, and the client reports stable reconnect semantics.
